assertion: The new EPA findings mark the last installment of tests ... UCMR 5, the regulation that required U.S. water utilities to test drinking water for 29 individual PFAS compounds.
reason: EPA released the final UCMR 5 dataset in August 2026 (Aug 27) covering 29 PFAS plus lithium, sampled 2023-2025. The article calls it new in November; it is nearly three months old.
independent_value: Final dataset released August 2026; 29 PFAS plus lithium

assertion: The agency is in the final stages of rolling back limits on four PFAS chemicals.
inaccuracy: EPA's May 18, 2026 action is a proposed rule; comment closed July 20, 2026 and no final rescission rule appears on EPA pages. 'Final stages' overstates procedural status.
reason: EPA pages describe a proposed rescission of PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and the Hazard Index mixture (incl. PFBS).
independent_value: EPA page: proposed rule announced May 18, 2026; comment period closed July 20, 2026

assertion: The agency plans to retain the PFOA and PFOS standards at 4 parts per trillion. But it also wants to extend the compliance deadline for meeting those standards to 2031.
inaccuracy: Proposal gives systems an option to request two additional years (to April 2031), not a blanket extension of the deadline from April 2029.
reason: EPA extension-rule page confirms 4.0 ppt unchanged and the 2031 option.
independent_value: 4.0 ppt unchanged; optional 2-year extension to April 2031
